mechanism_narrative: A sustained 5-month decline in the GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 2.5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of sustained GDPC1 decline below 2.5% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 3.5% signals an acceleration in supply-side activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in periods of sustained INDPRO acceleration above 3.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased discount rates applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of sustained FEDFUNDS rise above 4.5% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of sustained UNRATE rise above 5.5% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
